title: Binance Security Incident: What Happened and Why Custody Security Matters
summary: The October 29, 2026, Binance security incident resulted in approximately $6.3 billion in reported unauthorized withdrawals.

## Key Takeaways


-


The October 29, 2026, Binance security incident resulted in approximately $6.3 billion in reported unauthorized withdrawals, highlighting the risks associated with compromised transaction infrastructure.


-


Based on BitGo’s review to date BitGo was not impacted by the incident. Client assets remain secure, and operations continue normally across the platform.


-


Protecting digital assets requires more than securing private keys. Independent authorization, transaction policies, and withdrawal restrictions can help prevent unauthorized transfers or limit potential losses when access is compromised.


-


BitGo combines regulated qualified custody, cold storage, and configurable security controls with off-exchange settlement capabilities that allow investors to trade on participating exchanges while keeping supported assets in qualified custody.


On October 29, 2026, Binance[reported](https://x.com/binance/status/2115993361517891592) approximately $6.3 billion in unauthorized withdrawals after attackers compromised infrastructure associated with its hot wallets. While the investigation remains ongoing, Binance has reported finding no evidence to date that wallet private keys were leaked, raising broader questions about how digital asset transactions are authorized and secured.


Binance is a valued BitGo partner, and we continue to monitor developments as the investigation progresses. Based on BitGo’s review to date, BitGo was not impacted by the incident. Client assets remain secure, and operations continue normally across the platform.


The incident underscores the importance of looking beyond private-key security when evaluating how digital assets are protected. Custody arrangements, transaction approval processes, and withdrawal controls all influence how effectively investors can safeguard their holdings. For investors who also need access to exchange liquidity, separating trading activity from asset custody can provide another layer of protection.


## What Happened in the Binance Security Incident?


The attack targeted infrastructure associated with Binance's hot wallets, which rely on internet-connected systems to process transactions and withdrawals. While this connectivity supports efficient exchange operations, it also creates potential entry points for attackers seeking access to the systems and credentials involved in moving assets.


According to Binance's[initial investigation](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/c5a8729a97ac486d963784d96c5642d7) , a potentially compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer may have provided attackers with access to a service container involved in submitting withdrawals. Binance subsequently identified additional points of compromise, indicating that the attack was not necessarily limited to a single device.


Attackers do not necessarily need to steal private keys to cause unauthorized transactions. If they gain sufficient control over systems permitted to request or facilitate withdrawals, they may be able to exploit legitimate transaction processes. The precise sequence of events and the security controls affected by the Binance incident remain under investigation.


Following the discovery, Binance suspended withdrawals while conducting security checks, revoked affected authorizations, and began efforts to trace and freeze stolen assets.


By October 30, Binance reported that approximately $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen. Freezing assets can prevent further movement, although it does not necessarily mean those assets have been recovered.


Binance also committed to[covering customer losses](https://x.com/binance/status/2115981055043981791) through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and corporate resources, setting aside approximately $6.34 billion. By November 3, Binance said it had[replenished](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/binance-co-ceo-teng-says-hackers-used-fake-job-interviews-to-steal-6point3-billion-in-crypto.html) approximately 98% of the affected assets. The remaining portion is being purchased on the market and over the counter, and includes less liquid tokens.


By November 2, Binance had begun restoring withdrawals in phases, and the FBI had attributed the attack to the[North Korea-linked TraderTraitor group](https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/binance-sees-outflows-stabilising-exchange-returns-online-after-63-billion-heist-2026-11-02/) .


## Why Protecting Private Keys Isn't Enough


Private keys provide the cryptographic authority needed to sign digital asset transactions. Protecting them is fundamental to custody security, but investors also rely on account credentials, devices, applications, and transaction approval processes to access and manage their holdings.


When an investor keeps assets on an exchange, the exchange generally controls the private keys and the systems responsible for processing withdrawals. The investor can request a transfer, but the exchange's infrastructure ultimately determines how that request is authorized and executed.


For example, an attacker who compromises an account or system with permission to initiate withdrawals may be able to submit unauthorized transaction requests. If that access also provides sufficient authority to approve and execute transactions, assets could potentially be moved without the attacker directly obtaining the underlying private keys. Even when additional authorization is required, attackers may attempt to compromise the systems or credentials responsible for approving transactions.


A secure custody architecture therefore needs to address multiple stages of a transaction. Initiating a withdrawal, approving it, and signing the resulting transaction are distinct functions. Separating those responsibilities can reduce the risk that a single compromised account or device will be sufficient to move assets.


Transaction policies provide another layer of protection. Restrictions on withdrawal destinations, transaction amounts, and approval authority can limit what a compromised account is permitted to do. These controls are particularly valuable when they are enforced independently of the system or user initiating the transaction.


For individual investors, these considerations extend beyond the security of their exchange passwords or the use of two-factor authentication. Account-level safeguards remain important, but they cannot independently protect against every vulnerability within the infrastructure holding their assets.


## How BitGo's Qualified Custody Infrastructure Protects Digital Assets


BitGo's[regulated qualified custody](https://www.bitgo.com/products/qualified-custody/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=custody&utm_campaign=binance_security_incident) combines secure private-key storage with independent authorization and configurable transaction policies. These safeguards are designed to protect both the assets held in custody and the processes through which those assets can be moved.


For individual investors, qualified custody provides an alternative to holding assets directly on an exchange or managing private keys themselves. BitGo makes the security infrastructure developed for institutional digital assets available to individuals seeking professional custody.


### Regulated Qualified Custody


Choosing where to hold digital assets involves more than evaluating wallet security. Investors should also understand who holds their assets, how those assets are segregated, and what happens if a service provider experiences financial difficulties.


[BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A.](https://www.bitgo.com/company/licenses/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=custody&utm_campaign=binance_security_incident) is a federally chartered national trust bank supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC). Its qualified custody services provide a regulated framework for safeguarding client digital assets.


BitGo's custody model keeps client assets segregated from the custodian's own holdings, with protections designed to safeguard those assets if the custodian experiences financial difficulties. Insurance provides another layer of protection against certain types of losses, although coverage depends on the policy's terms, limits, and exclusions.


These safeguards are designed to address risks that technical wallet security alone cannot resolve, including how client assets are held and protected if a custodian encounters financial difficulties.


### Cold Storage and Independent Authorization


Cold storage reduces exposure to attacks against internet-connected infrastructure by keeping sensitive private-key material offline.


BitGo's[qualified custody offering](https://www.bitgo.com/products/qualified-custody/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=custody&utm_campaign=binance_security_incident) uses cold storage and isolated signing environments to protect the keys responsible for authorizing asset movements. Rather than exposing those keys directly to online transaction systems, signing takes place within a controlled custody environment.


Independent authorization adds another layer of security by separating the ability to request a transaction from the authority required to approve and complete it.


Withdrawal requests can require independent approvals or signing controls before assets move. These safeguards help prevent a compromised online account or operational system from independently authorizing transfers, even if an attacker gains the ability to submit transaction requests.


### Transaction Policies


BitGo's[policy engine](https://www.bitgo.com/resource-center/bitgo-policies/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=custody&utm_campaign=binance_security_incident) allows clients to establish rules governing transaction activity and control what users and systems are permitted to do.


Policies can restrict withdrawal destinations, establish approval requirements, control user permissions, and limit transaction amounts over defined periods. Available controls vary by wallet and product.


[Velocity controls](https://www.bitgo.com/products/custody-wallets/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=custody&utm_campaign=binance_security_incident) can help limit the amount of value transferred within a specified period. For example, a policy might restrict the total value of withdrawals over a defined time window, limiting how much could be transferred even if an unauthorized transaction request were submitted.


Other policies can require additional authorization for transactions above established thresholds or restrict transfers to previously approved addresses. Together, these controls establish boundaries around when, where, and how digital assets can be moved.


These protections are only as strong as their configuration and enforcement. Access to modify transaction policies must also be secured, since an attacker with sufficient administrative permissions could attempt to change withdrawal restrictions.


### Trading and Settlement From Qualified Custody


Investors who want to trade traditionally have had to transfer assets onto exchanges to access liquidity, placing those holdings within the exchange's custody infrastructure. Off-exchange settlement provides an alternative by separating trading execution from asset custody.


Through[Go Network's off-exchange settlement](https://www.bitgo.com/products/go-network-oes/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=custody&utm_campaign=binance_security_incident) , institutions can allocate supported assets for trading on participating exchanges while keeping those assets in BitGo's regulated qualified custody. Trades execute on participating exchanges, with settlement handled through Go Network.


This allows investors to access exchange liquidity without holding the same assets directly on an exchange, reducing exposure to risks associated with exchange custody. Off-exchange settlement does not eliminate counterparty, trading, or operational risk, but it allows investors to separate the infrastructure used to execute trades from the infrastructure responsible for safeguarding their assets.


## Building a More Resilient Digital Asset Infrastructure


The Binance incident suggests that digital asset security depends on more than protecting private keys. How transactions are authorized, what restrictions govern withdrawals, and where assets are held all influence an investor's exposure to operational and security risks. Independent custody and controls that separate transaction requests from signing authority can provide additional safeguards when systems are compromised.


BitGo brings regulated qualified custody, cold storage, independent authorization, and configurable transaction controls together on one platform. Through Go Network, clients can also trade on participating exchanges while keeping supported assets in qualified custody. The same institutional-grade custody infrastructure is available to eligible individual investors seeking to safeguard their digital assets without managing their own private keys or recovery phrases.

## FAQs


### What happened in the Binance security incident?


On October 29, 2026, Binance reported approximately $6.3 billion in unauthorized withdrawals following a compromise of infrastructure associated with its hot wallets. The exchange suspended withdrawals, investigated the attack, and began tracing and freezing stolen assets. Binance reported no evidence to date that wallet private keys had been leaked, although the full sequence of events remains under investigation.


### Were BitGo assets affected by the Binance security incident?


No. Based on BitGo’s review to date, BitGo was not impacted by the Binance security incident. Client assets remain secure, and operations continue normally across the platform. BitGo's qualified custody infrastructure operates independently of exchange custody systems, with safeguards designed to protect digital assets and control how transactions are authorized.


### Can cryptocurrency be stolen without compromising private keys?


Yes. Attackers may be able to initiate unauthorized withdrawals by compromising accounts, applications, or infrastructure involved in processing transactions. If those systems have sufficient authority to approve and execute transfers, assets can potentially be moved without attackers directly obtaining private keys. Independent transaction approvals, withdrawal restrictions, and access controls help reduce this risk.


### Is it safer to hold cryptocurrency in cold storage or on an exchange?


Cold storage reduces exposure to attacks against internet-connected systems by keeping sensitive private-key material offline. Exchanges typically use online infrastructure to support trading and withdrawals, creating different operational risks. However, cold storage alone does not guarantee absolute security. Investors should also evaluate who controls their assets, how transactions are approved, and what protections exist against unauthorized withdrawals.


### Can investors trade cryptocurrency without keeping assets on an exchange?


Yes. Off-exchange settlement allows eligible investors to access exchange liquidity while keeping supported assets with an independent custodian. Through BitGo's Go Network, institutions can trade on participating exchanges while their allocated assets remain in regulated qualified custody. This reduces exposure to exchange custody risk without eliminating trading, counterparty, or operational risks.
